correctness.rationale: Generator images parameterize all derivations, with the relation t^n=0 checked separately for each parity. In characteristic two D squared is again a derivation, so the necessary-and-sufficient equations are exactly ab=b squared=0 in the length-m truncated ring. Truncated valuations give all distinct reduced irreducible linear components and their intersections; inclusion by adjacent components gives the count. The valuation of the image generator proves rank and acyclicity. Independent exhaustive matrix reconstruction agrees in 16 finite configurations over GF(2), GF(4). Scheme-theoretic nilpotents are deliberately excluded.

value.rationale: The restricted 2-nilpotent cone of a truncated-ring derivation Lie algebra is a natural geometric invariant. The theorem completely classifies its reduced components for every truncation length, reveals a non-obvious equality and rank-preserving linear isomorphism between adjacent even/odd lengths, and gives arithmetic and homological consequences including an unbounded number of components and an exact acyclic stratum. These facts go beyond an arbitrary isolated coefficient test or known nilpotent-matrix enumeration.
